meta.title: {{name}} · Transitions for Minecraft Video Creators
meta.description: Pick a template, tune a few parameters, preview at 60 fps, and export alpha-channel clips ready to drop onto your editing timeline. Free, open source, and offline.

hero.lead: {{name}} is a desktop app: pick a template, tune a few parameters, preview live at 60 fps, and export transparent clips ready to drop onto your timeline.
hero.worldHint: Brush through the voxel {{mascot}} above, or drag floating blocks near each other to snap them together
hero.noWebgl: WebGL2 is unavailable in this browser, so the live engine preview cannot start.
hero.engineFailed: Live render engine failed to start. Reload to retry.
hero.mcAssets: Block and item textures on this site are extracted from Minecraft {{version}} (© Mojang / Microsoft) for showcase only; the desktop app reads your local game and resource packs, with zero game files bundled in the installer.
hero.demoAssets: This page is using procedural demo swatches; the desktop app reads your local Minecraft installation and resource packs directly.

story.title: From launch to export in three steps.
story.lead: Design goal: under 30 seconds from opening the app to exporting your first transition. The monitor beside you renders live as all three steps play out—or click any tab.

exportStages.rendering: Rendering frame by frame (with subframe motion blur)…

pick.title: Pick a template.
pick.body: Transitions or HUD overlays. Every frame you see is rendered live right now in your browser.
pick.more: Full template library & pack import in the desktop app

tune.title: Tune a few knobs.
tune.body: Columns, entry pattern, spin, blocks—every adjustment lands on the very next frame from controls generated directly out of manifest.json.

export.title: Export and drop onto your cut.
export.body: Choose codec, resolution, and frame rate. Every exported frame matches the preview; align the cut marker to the seam between two clips.

cut.body: What just wiped across your screen was the "{{template}}" template itself—rendered live by the same engine across the seam between two sections, just like on an editing timeline.

sim.title: Identical to the desktop app—right in your browser.
sim.lead: Inside this window runs the actual desktop editor UI and real-time WebGL engine—not a mockup. Jump between signature templates above, scrub the multi-segment timeline, tweak inspector controls, or test-run Export.
sim.autoStart: Automatically boots when scrolled into view
sim.exportNote: The browser workbench executes the full frame-by-frame render rehearsal; writing ProRes 4444 / WebM / PNG files on disk is handled by FFmpeg in the desktop app.
sim.compact: The full multi-pane desktop editor requires a wider screen (≥ 900px). On mobile, switch templates and scrub the live engine right here:

templates.title: Start with a few signature pieces.
templates.lead: Every card is rendered in your browser by the real engine. Hover to play the loop, or open any template directly inside the 1:1 desktop editor above.
templates.moreBody: The desktop app ships a rich collection of transitions and Minecraft HUD overlays, plus an SDK for authoring deterministic custom templates.

features.title: Every detail shaped around video editing.

alpha.title: True alpha channel export
alpha.body: Drop clips straight onto an upper video track with zero chroma-keying. Drag the divider to compare raw transparency against scene compositing.

frames.title: Preview equals final render
frames.body: Every frame is a pure function of time. Preview and export run the exact same code path frame-for-frame, with optional subframe motion blur.

formats.title: Formats editors actually expect
formats.body: Straight/premultiplied alpha codecs for NLE timelines, plus green-screen H.264 for lightweight editors.

apps.prores: Premiere Pro · DaVinci Resolve · Final Cut Pro · After Effects
apps.png: Any NLE or compositing software supporting image sequences
apps.webm: OBS Studio · Premiere Pro · DaVinci Resolve · Web overlays
apps.greenscreen: CapCut · mobile editors & timelines without alpha tracks

stack.title: Bring your own resource packs
stack.body: A three-layer resource stack: built-in fallback colors, your local vanilla Minecraft jar, and your custom resource packs on top. Click any layer to inspect:

offline.title: Offline & Worker-sandboxed
offline.body: No accounts, telemetry, or analytics. Template scripts execute inside an isolated Web Worker with all network and DOM globals stripped:

extend.title: Declare a parameter, get a control
extend.body: Presets, derived templates, portable template packs, and TypeScript modules. One parameter entry in manifest.json automatically becomes an inspector control:

open.title: Free, open source, built in the open.
open.lead: Source code is available on GitHub under GPL-3.0. Issues, custom templates, and pull requests are welcome.
